title: Every moment is baptism's time, Easter most of all
english: The wise Solomon, dividing up the times of life's affairs and setting aside the right moment for each thing that happens, said: "There is a time for everything, and a season for every matter: a time to be born, and a time to die" (Ecclesiastes 3:1-2). But I would alter the wise man's saying just a little, and proclaim to you the saving message: there is a time to die, and a time to be born.

Why this change? Because he was speaking about things that come into being and pass away, following bodily nature, and so he placed birth before death—for no one can experience death without first being born. But I am about to speak of spiritual rebirth, and so I place death before life. For by dying to the flesh we gain birth in the Spirit, as the Lord also says: "I kill, and I make alive" (Deuteronomy 32:39). Let us die, then, so that we may live. Let us put to death the sinful nature, which cannot submit to God's law, so that the mindset of the Spirit may grow strong in us—the mindset through which life and peace naturally come. Let us be buried with Christ, who died for us, so that we may also rise with Him who secured our resurrection.

Different times suit different things: there is a time for sleep and a time for waking, a time for war and a time for peace. But for baptism, the entire life of human beings is the time. A body cannot live without breathing, and a soul cannot hold together without knowing its Creator. Ignorance of God is the death of the soul. And the unbaptized person has not been enlightened. Without light, an eye cannot see what belongs to it, nor can a soul receive the contemplation of God.

Every moment, then, offers the opportunity for salvation through baptism—whether you name night or day, an hour or an instant, or the very briefest point of time. But surely the moment most closely related to baptism is the most fitting. What could be more akin to baptism than the day of Easter? That day is the memorial of the resurrection, and baptism is the power that leads to resurrection. On the day of resurrection, then, let us receive the grace of the resurrection. This is why the Church calls her nurslings together from afar with a loud proclamation, so that those for whom she long labored in birth she may bring forth on that day—and having weaned them from the words of instruction, she may give them a taste of the solid food of the teachings.

John the Baptist preached a baptism of repentance, and all Judea went out to him. The Lord preaches a baptism of adoption—and who among those who have hoped in Him will not obey? That baptism was introductory; this one brings to completion. That one was a withdrawal from sin; this one is a kinship with God. John the Baptist's preaching was that of one man, and it drew everyone to repentance. But you—taught through the prophets, "Wash yourselves; become clean" (Isaiah 1:16); admonished through the psalms, "Come to Him, and be enlightened" (Psalm 34:6); evangelized through the apostles, "Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins, and you will receive the promise of the Holy Spirit" (Acts 2:38); welcomed by the Lord Himself, who says, "Come to me, all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest" (Matthew 11:28)—for all these readings have come together today—do you still hesitate, deliberate, and keep delaying?

You have been instructed in the word since infancy, and you have not yet committed yourself to the truth? Always learning, and you have not yet come to knowledge? A tester your whole life, a spy until old age—when will you become a Christian? When will we recognize you as one of us? Last year you were waiting for this present season; now you are waiting again for the next one.
orientation: Basil opens his homily by reworking Solomon's saying about times, arguing that the whole of human life is the season for baptism, and that Easter, as the day of resurrection, is the most fitting moment to receive it.

title: The Yoke of Christ and the True Baptism
english: Take care that you are not making promises that reach beyond your life. You do not know what the coming day will bring (Proverbs 27:1); do not promise what is not yours. We are calling you to life, my friend—why do you flee from the call? We are calling you to a share in good things—why do you pass over the gift? The kingdom of heaven stands open; the One who calls does not lie; the road is easy, with no need of time, expense, or trouble. Why do you delay? Why do you shrink back? Why do you fear the yoke like a heifer unaccustomed to the yoke? It is good, it is light; it does not chafe the neck but gives it glory. For the yoke-strap is not bound around the neck; it seeks the one who draws it of his own free will. Do you see how Ephraim is accused as a heifer driven to frenzy, because she wanders in disorder, dishonoring the yoke of the law? Put your untamed neck under it; become a beast of burden for Christ, so that, loosed from the yoke and living without restraint, you may not be easy prey for wild beasts. “Taste and see that the Lord is good” (Psalm 34:8). How can I announce the sweetness of honey to those who do not know it? Taste and see. Experience is clearer than any word for making a proof. The Jew does not postpone circumcision because of the threat: “Every soul that is not circumcised on the eighth day shall be cut off from its people” (Genesis 17:14). But you put off the circumcision not made by hands, which is brought to completion in baptism, in the stripping off of the flesh—even though you have heard the Lord Himself say, “Truly, truly, I say to you, unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God” (John 3:5). There, there is pain and a wound; here, there is dew for the soul and healing for the wound of the heart. Do you worship the One who died for you? Then accept being buried with Him through baptism. If you are not united with the likeness of His death, how will you share in His resurrection (Romans 6:5)? That Israel was baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea (1 Corinthians 10:2), handing down to you the types and marking out the truth that would be shown in the last times. But you altogether shun baptism—not one prefigured in the sea, but one brought to completion in truth; not in the cloud, but in the Spirit; not into Moses, your fellow servant, but into Christ, the Maker. If Israel had not passed through the sea, they would not have been separated from Pharaoh; and you, if you do not pass through the water, will not be separated from the bitter tyranny of the devil. They would not have drunk from the spiritual rock if they had not been baptized in type (1 Corinthians 10:4); and no one will give you the true drink unless you are truly baptized. They ate the bread of angels after baptism (Psalm 78:25); how will you eat the living bread unless you first receive baptism? They entered the land of promise through baptism; how will you return to paradise unless you are sealed with baptism? Or do you not know that a flaming sword has been set to guard the way to the tree of life (Genesis 3:24)—fearsome and blazing for the faithless, but for those who have believed, approachable and shining with lovely light? And the Master made it turn: when it sees a believer, it gives its back; but when it sees one of the unsealed, it meets him face to face.
orientation: Basil continues his direct address to the delaying hearer, urging immediate baptism by contrasting the easy yoke of Christ with the danger of remaining unbaptized.

title: Elijah's water kindles fire; grace offered, excuses made
english: Elijah was not terrified when a chariot of fire and horses of fire came to him; he longed for the journey upward, and so he dared those fearful things. With great joy he mounted the flaming vehicle while still living in the flesh. But you are not about to mount a chariot of fire; you are about to ascend to heaven through water and the Spirit—and you do not run to the call? Elijah showed the power of baptism at the altar of whole burnt offerings, when he consumed the sacrifice not with fire but with water. By nature fire and water are at war with each other, but when the water was mystically poured over the altar a third time, it became the starting point for the fire and kindled the flame as if it were oil. “Take jars,” he says, “and pour water on the whole burnt offering and on the pieces of wood.” And he said, “Do it a second time,” and they did it a second time. “Do it a third time,” and they did it a third time (1 Kings 18:33-34). The word shows that through baptism the one who comes forward is made a member of God's household, and that pure, heavenly light shines forth in the souls of those who approach through faith in the Trinity. If I were distributing gold to the church, you would not say to me, “I will come tomorrow, and tomorrow you will give it.” You would demand the distribution at once, pressing me, and you would be annoyed at any delay. But since the great giver is offering you not the fine color of matter but the purity of your soul, you invent pretexts and count up excuses when you ought to run to the gift. What a wonder! You are renewed, without being melted down; you are reshaped, without being broken; you are healed, without suffering pain—and you do not reckon the grace. If you were a slave of human beings, and freedom had been proclaimed for slaves, would you not have gone to meet the lady, hiring advocates and pleading with judges, so that by every means you might be delivered into freedom? Surely you would even have accepted a slap on the face—the last blow a slave receives—to be rid of the abuses that would follow. But now you are a slave, not of human beings, but of sin, and the herald calls you to freedom, to release you from captivity, to make you a fellow citizen with the angels, to show you as a son of God adopted through grace, and an heir of the good things of Christ—and you still say it is not yet the time for you to receive what is being given. What wicked obstacles! What shameful, endless busyness! How long will pleasures last? How long will luxuries last? We have lived a long time for the world; let us live from now on for ourselves. What is worth as much as the soul? What weighs equally with the kingdom of heaven? Who is a more trustworthy counselor to you than God? Who is wiser than the wise one? Who is more helpful than the good one? Who is closer to you than the Creator? It did not benefit Eve to obey the serpent's counsel rather than the Master's. What absurd words! “I have no leisure to be made well; do not show me the light yet; do not unite me to the King yet.” Is this not what you are saying outright? Or rather, things even more irrational than these. If your name had been written in the public debt records, and a cancellation of debts had been announced to those who owed, and then someone tried out of malice to keep you from sharing in that pardon, you would be outraged and you would cry out that he was robbing you of your portion of the common grace.
orientation: Basil is still addressing those who delay baptism, now using Elijah's water-drenched sacrifice as a figure of baptism's power and then confronting the hearer's excuses directly.

title: Baptism's gifts and the seal that marks God's own
english: But since not only forgiveness of the past has been proclaimed beforehand, but also gifts of the future, you are wronging yourself in ways not even one of your enemies would have spitefully done to you, and yet you think you have planned well and reasoned profitably about yourself. You refuse the forgiveness and die in your debts. And you know this: the debtor of ten thousand talents would have received forgiveness, if he had not renewed the demand for payment against himself by his cruelty toward his fellow servant (Matthew 18:23-35). We must be careful not to suffer the same thing once we have received grace, by not forgiving our own debtors, so that the gift may remain secure for us.

Enter the inner chamber of your soul, and stir up the memory of what you have done. If your sins are many, do not be discouraged by their number. For where sin increased, grace increased all the more (Romans 5:20), if you accept the grace. The one who owes much will have much forgiven, so that he may love more (Luke 7:47). But if your sins are small and trivial, and not leading to death, why are you anxious about the future, when you bore the past not ignobly, and that without yet being trained by the law?

Now consider your soul as standing on a balance, pulled from one side by angels and from the other by demons. To which will you give the weight of your heart? What will win in you: pleasure of the flesh, or holiness of the soul? Enjoyment of present things, or desire for the things to come? Will angels receive you, or will those who hold you keep their grip?

In battle, generals distribute a watchword to their troops, so that friends can easily call to one another, and so that when they are mixed with the enemy in close combat, the separation can be clearly made. No one will recognize whether you are one of ours or one of the enemy, unless you show your allegiance through the mystical symbols, unless the light of the Lord's face is marked upon you (Numbers 6:25). How will the angel claim you? How will he snatch you from the enemy, if he does not recognize the seal? How will you say, "I belong to God," if you do not carry the marks of identification?

Or do you not know that the destroyer passed over the houses that were sealed, but in the unsealed houses he slaughtered the firstborn (Exodus 12:23)? An unsealed treasure is easy prey for thieves; an unmarked sheep is plotted against without risk.

Are you young? Secure your youth with the bridle of baptism. Has your prime passed? Do not be deprived of the provisions for the journey; do not lose the amulet; do not think about the eleventh hour as if it were the first. For it is fitting even for the one beginning life to keep the end before his eyes.

If one of the doctors promised you that by some devices and contrivances he would make you young from old, would you not long for that day to come, when you were about to see yourself returning to your prime? But when baptism promises to make your soul flourish again—the soul you have made old, and which it promises to rescue from lawlessness, though you have shown it stained—you despise your benefactor and do not run to the promise.

Do you not desire to see what the great wonder of the promise is? How is a person reborn without a mother? How does the one who is growing old and being corrupted according to the desires of deceit become vigorous again, and return to youth, and come back to the true flower of young manhood?

Baptism is ransom for captives, forgiveness of debts, death of sin, regeneration of the soul, a garment of light, a seal that cannot be assailed, a vehicle to heaven, the means of gaining the kingdom, the gift of adoption.
orientation: Basil is addressing those who delay baptism, now arguing that baptism not only forgives past sins but also grants future gifts, and that the baptized person must be marked with God's seal to be recognized and protected.

title: The hidden logic of delaying baptism
english: Wretched one, do you really rank pleasure above goods so many and so great? I understand your postponement, even if you cover it over with words. The facts themselves cry out, even if your voice is silent. "Let me use my flesh for the enjoyment of shameful things; let me wallow in the mire of pleasures; let me stain my hands with blood, take what belongs to others, walk in deceit, swear falsely, lie—and then, when I finally stop doing evil, I will receive baptism." If sin is good, then keep it to the end. But if it harms the one who does it, why do you persist in what destroys you? No one who wants to vomit up bile first gathers more of it into himself through a bad and dissolute diet. You should cleanse the body of what troubles it, not make the disease greater than your strength. A ship shows how much weight of cargo it can bear; anything beyond that sinks it. Be afraid that you may suffer the same thing—that by making your sins greater than the forgiveness, you may suffer shipwreck before the hoped-for harbor. Does God not see what happens? Does He not understand your thoughts? Does He cooperate with you in your lawless deeds? You thought that I would be just like you, He says (Psalm 49:21). When you seek the friendship of a mortal man, you win him over with good deeds, saying and doing the things you know please him. But when you are drawing near to God and hoping to be received into the rank of a son, you do what is hostile to God and dishonor Him by breaking the law—and from the very things that most offend Him, you hope for closeness? Watch out: if you pile up a mass of evils for yourself in hope of redemption, you may gather sin and yet miss the forgiveness. God is not mocked (Galatians 6:7). Do not trade in the grace. Do not say, "The law is good, but sin is sweeter." Pleasure is the devil's fishhook, dragging you to destruction. Pleasure is the mother of sin, and sin is the sting of death (1 Corinthians 15:56). Pleasure is the nurse of the eternal worm: for a time it soothes the one who enjoys it, but afterward it produces a bitterness sharper than gall. Your postponement cries out nothing other than this: "Let sin reign in me first, and then one day the Lord will reign. Let me present my members as weapons of unrighteousness to lawlessness, and then one day I will present them as weapons of righteousness to God." That is how Cain offered his sacrifices: the first things to his own enjoyment, the second to God who created and gave them. While you are strong in deeds, you spend your youth on sins. When your organs are worn out, then you bring them to God—when they are good for nothing, when they must lie idle because their strength has been paralyzed by the decay of time. Self-control in old age is not self-control; it is inability for licentiousness. A corpse is not crowned. No one is righteous merely through being unable to do evil. As long as you have strength, master sin by your will. For this is virtue: turning away from evil and doing good. But mere inactivity in wickedness deserves neither praise nor punishment on its own. If you stop sinning because of age, the credit belongs to weakness. We praise those who are good by choice, not those who are kept from evil by some necessity.
orientation: Basil is addressing the hearer who postpones baptism, exposing the unspoken reasoning behind the delay and answering it with warnings about sin, pleasure, and the danger of presuming on God's forgiveness.

title: The Devil's Trick of Delay
english: Who has fixed the limit of your life? Who has defined the deadline of your old age? Who is such a trustworthy guarantor to you of what is to come? Do you not see infants being snatched away, those in their prime being carried off? Life has no single deadline. Why do you wait for baptism to come to you as a gift of fever—when you will not be able to utter the saving words, and perhaps will not even be permitted to hear clearly, with the sickness dwelling in your very head? You will not be able to raise your hands to heaven, or stand up on your feet, or bend the knee in worship, or be taught usefully, or confess securely, or make your covenant with God, or renounce the enemy—perhaps not even to follow the initiation with understanding, yourself uncertain whether you have perceived the grace or are insensible to what is happening. And even if you do receive the grace with awareness, then you have the talent but you bring no work to it. Imitate the eunuch. He found the one who instructed him, and he did not despise the teaching. The rich man brought the poor man up onto his chariot—the dignified and exalted man brought up the ordinary and despised man. And when he was taught the gospel of the kingdom, he received the faith in his heart, but he did not postpone the seal of the Spirit. For when they came upon water, he said, 'Look, water!' The word came from overflowing joy: 'Look—the thing I was seeking! What prevents me from being baptized?' Where the will is ready, nothing prevents. For the one who calls is loving toward humanity, the minister is prepared, the grace is abundant. Let eagerness be present, and there will be no obstacle. There is one who prevents, one who blocks our roads to salvation—let us overcome him by understanding. He produces hesitation in us; let us rise up to the work. He deceives our hearts with empty promises; let us not be ignorant of his schemes. For does he not suggest that we commit sin today, and persuade us to store up righteousness for tomorrow? This is why the Lord, dismantling his wicked counsels, says, 'Today, if you hear my voice' (Psalm 94:7 (95:7)). That one says: 'Give today to me, and tomorrow to God.' The Lord cries out in answer: 'Today, hear my voice.' Understand the enemy: he does not dare to advise abandoning God altogether—he knows that is hard for Christians to hear—but he schemes against the undertaking with deceptive arts. He is clever at doing evil. He observes that we human beings live in the present, and every action is carried out in the present moment. So by stealing our today through his scheming, he leaves us the hopes of tomorrow. Then, when tomorrow comes, the wicked divider comes again, claiming today for himself and tomorrow for the Lord. And so, always snatching away the present through pleasure and attaching the future to our hopes, he secretly leads us astray from life. I once saw such cunning in a clever bird. Since her chicks were easy to catch because of their softness, she offered herself as ready prey, turning about in the hands of the hunters. She was neither easily caught by them, nor did she make them despair of the hunt. Instead, holding them with varied hopes by keeping them occupied with herself, she won her chicks the chance to escape—and then at last she herself was caught.
orientation: Basil is addressing those who postpone baptism, now exposing the devil's strategy of stealing today for sin while promising tomorrow to God.

title: Enroll now; the narrow way is worth its cost
english: Be afraid that you too may suffer something similar, surrendering what is clear in hopes about what is uncertain. Come then, transfer your whole self to the Lord. Give your name. Be enrolled with the Church. The soldier is counted in the muster rolls; the athlete competes after being registered; the citizen, once enrolled as a citizen, is counted among his tribesmen. You are liable to all these things: as a soldier of Christ, as an athlete of godliness, as one having citizenship in the heavens. Be registered in this book, so that you may be transferred to the one above. Learn, be taught the gospel way of life: precision of the eyes, restraint of the tongue, enslavement of the body, a humble mindset, purity of thoughts, the destruction of anger. When pressed into service, add more; when robbed, do not go to court; when hated, love; when persecuted, endure; when reviled, speak kindly. Be put to death to sin; be crucified with Christ; transfer your whole love to the Lord.

But these things are hard. What good thing is easy? Who has set up a trophy while sleeping? Who has been adorned with the crowns of endurance while living in luxury and being serenaded by flutes? No one has taken the prize without running. Labors give birth to glory; toils procure crowns. “Through many tribulations we must enter the kingdom of heaven” (Acts 14:22), I say too. But these tribulations are awaited by the blessedness in the kingdom of heaven, while the painful and gloomy toil of Gehenna awaits the toils of sin.

And yet, for one who examines carefully, not even the works of the devil come to the workers of lawlessness without toil. What are the sweats of self-control? But the fornicator is drenched in sweat, as pleasure wastes him away. Does self-control take away as much from the body as foul and raging licentiousness destroys? The nights of those who pass the night in prayers are sleepless; but far harsher are the nights of those who stay awake in injustices. For the fear of being caught and the frenzy of pleasures drive away all rest completely.

But if, fleeing the narrowness of the road that leads to salvation, you pursue the broad way of sin, I fear that, having traveled the wide road to the end, you may find the lodging that matches the road. So the treasure is hard to guard. Keep watch, brother. You have helpers, if you wish: prayer keeping the night watch, fasting staying at home, psalmody refreshing the soul. Take these along with you. Let them keep watch with you over the guarding of what is precious. What is better, tell me: for us to be rich and to strive on behalf of the guarding of what is precious, or not to have from the start what we would guard? No one pushes away good things out of fear of being deprived of them. For in that way nothing human would have been established, if we calculated the failures for each of our pursuits. For farming has barrenness lying beside it, trade has shipwrecks, marriages have widowhoods, child-rearing has childlessness. But nevertheless we set our hands to the works, leaning on the better hopes, and we entrust the outcome of what we hoped for to the God who orders our affairs.

But you praise sanctification in word, yet in deed you linger in condemned things. See to it that you never regret your evil counsels, when regret will be of no use to you. Let the example of the virgins correct you. They did not have oil in their vessels, and when they needed to enter with the bridegroom, then they perceived that they lacked what was necessary (Matthew 25:1-13).
orientation: Basil has just compared the devil's delaying tactics to a mother bird's trick, and now turns directly to the hearer with an urgent call to enroll for baptism and to accept the discipline of the Christian life.

title: The Lament of the Unbaptized at Death
english: That is why the word called them foolish: they spent the time for using their oil on going around and trading, and without realizing it they shut themselves out of the brightness of the bridal chamber. Take care that you too, postponing year after year, month after month, day after day, and not taking the oil, the food of light, never fall into a day you do not expect, when the means of living finally fail you. Then there is helplessness on every side and grief no one can comfort: the doctors have given up, your family has given up. When you are gripped by rapid, dry gasping, while a fierce fever burns and smolders within you, you will groan from the depths of your heart and find no one to share your grief. You will utter something faint and feeble, and there will be no one to hear. Everything you say is dismissed as delirium. Who will give you baptism then? Who will remind you when you are stupefied by suffering? Your relatives are in despair; those outside the suffering think nothing of it; your friend hesitates to remind you, as it would cause distress. Perhaps the doctor deceives you too, and you do not despair of yourself because by nature you cling to life. Night, and a desert of helpers. The one who baptizes is not there. Death stands by; those who carry you off press on. Who is there to rescue you? God, whom you despised? But will he listen then? You are the one who is not listening to him now. Will he grant an extension? You made such good use of the time already given. Let no one deceive you with empty words. Sudden destruction will come upon you, and ruin will arrive like a storm. A grim angel will come, dragging you away by force and pulling your soul, bound fast by its sins, turning back again and again toward the things of this world, mourning without a voice, since the organ of lament now silenced. Oh, how you will tear at yourself! How you will groan, repenting uselessly over your deliberations, when you see the brightness of the righteous in the radiant distribution of gifts, and the gloom of sinners in the deepest darkness. What will you say then in the anguish of your heart? 'Woe is me, that I did not throw off this heavy burden of sin when laying it down was so easy, but instead dragged this heap of evils along with me. Woe is me, that I did not wash away the stains, but remained marked by my sins. Now I would have been with the angels; now I would have been delighting in the good things of heaven. Oh, wicked plans! For a temporary enjoyment of sin I am tortured forever; for the pleasure of the flesh I am handed over to the fire. God's judgment is just. I was called, and I did not obey. I was taught, and I paid no attention. They bore witness to me, and I laughed.' These things and others like them you will say, weeping over yourself, if you are snatched away before baptism. Man, either fear hell or lay claim to the kingdom. Do not dishonor the call. Do not say, 'Excuse me for this reason or that.' No excuse is sufficient for refusal. I am moved to tears when I consider that you prefer the works of shame to the great glory of God, and that because of the sweetness of self-indulgence you cling to sin so tightly that you cannot be pulled away, shutting yourself out from the good things promised, so that you never see the good things of the heavenly Jerusalem. There are myriads of angels, assemblies of the firstborn, thrones of apostles, seats of honor for prophets, scepters of patriarchs, crowns of martyrs, praises of the righteous. Long to be numbered among them, having washed yourself and been sanctified according to the gift of Christ. For to him be the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen.
orientation: Basil is addressing the hearer who keeps postponing baptism, and now imagines the scene of that person's death and the lament they will utter when it is too late.
